newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares stuck in starting blocks.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares stuck in starting blocks.

text.p: Belgian shares were held back on Tuesday morning by profit-taking in a handful of stocks after Monday's surge to new record levels, but the underlying trend remained bullish, dealers said.
"The elements -- low rates and speculation -- are still there, so the trend is still up," one said.

At 0835 GMT, the Bel-20 index was up 0.11 percent, or 2.46 points, at 2,281.50. It had been fired on Monday by a major reshuffle among holding companies Gevaert, Almanij and Cobepa, and speculation involving insurer Royale Belge and Kredietbank.
Gevaert, whose assets are to be shared out between Almanij and Cobepa in a complex series of transactions, was the leading loser with a 2.7 percent drop to 3,250 francs.
" A correction is logical, it's become too expensive," one trader said. Almanij was down 2.1 percent at 16,500.
Cobepa was down 1.3 percent at 1,500 but dealers said they still considered it a buy.

Royale Belge was up 0.1 percent at 9,950 francs, which had thrived in recent sessions on speculation it might be sold by its French parent AXA-UAP. The market was awaiting Royale Belge's shareholders meeting on Wednesday for news.
Kredietbank (KB) was up 0.3 percent at 14,450 francs on lingering speculation it would enter an alliance with a foreign partner sooner or later.
KB said last week it was in exploratory talks with Dutch co-operative bank Rabobank, and other companies it declined to name, as part of expansion plans.
"The buying interest in KB is likely to continue in the next few months," one dealer said.
